messages:
sam_support: Customer ACME reporting: after a traffic spike from EU clients they started getting garbled outputs and intermittent 502s. Also seeing a billing jump (lots of retries). They say requests target eu-west but logs show traffic routed to us-east standby. Can SRE help triage?

neha_sre: thanks — can you paste a sample request id and the response snippet? any logs showing which model variant actually served? :eyes:

sam_support: sample request id: rq_0ab9f3e2. Log snippet: ```
2026-03-16T14:22:11Z rq_0ab9f3e2 route=eu-west -> routed_to=us-east fallback_variant=redwood-lite-quant-v1 status=partial_response tokens_emitted=12 error="tokenizer_vocab_mismatch"
2026-03-16T14:22:11Z rq_0ab9f3e2 billing.tokens=12 retry=1
2026-03-16T14:22:12Z rq_0ab9f3e2 status=502 message="generation stream aborted"
```
Customer payload was standard chat/generate with short prompt. They retried on 502s which seems to have doubled token billing.

leo_prod: hmm — that fallback_variant is the key. We recently updated the standby map for eu-west to point to a smaller quantized lite variant as a cost/standby optimization. Looks like that variant uses a different tokenizer config (vocab size/offset) and is incompatible with the primary model family for some prompts.

sre-bot: [auto] failover event recorded: route-eu-west -> us-east at 2026-03-16T14:22:10Z. reason=capacity_shortage fallback_variant=redwood-lite-quant-v1 commit=6f9b2a dep=router-v2.3.1

neha_sre: reproduction attempt: hitting the eu-west router with header override to force failover yields the same garbling. quick repro curl: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "x-region-hint: eu-west" \n  -H "x-request-id: rq_repro_001" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-alpha","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize: Q1 results."}]}'
```
When routed to `redwood-lite-quant-v1` the first token mapping is off and we see `tokenizer_vocab_mismatch` in the runtime.

sam_support: customer also saw repeated partial outputs across retries (client retried on 502) — each attempt produced some tokens then aborted, which was billed. They want a credit and an explanation.

leo_prod: short-term mitigations: 1) add account-level route pin for ACME to prefer eu-west primary (avoid standby) 2) block fallback to any `*-lite-quant` variants for `generation` workloads until tokenizer compatibility is verified 3) rollback standby map change that introduced redwood-lite-quant-v1 for eu-west standby. I'll open a rollout revert.

neha_sre: medium-term: router should validate tokenizer metadata compatibility before allowing a variant swap. Proposed quick check in router pseudocode: ```py
def compatible(primary, candidate):
    return primary.tokenizer.digest == candidate.tokenizer.digest
if not compatible(primary, candidate):
    return 503, "incompatible-fallback"
```
Also adding a temporary metric/alert: failover_count && tokenizer_mismatch_count > 0 -> pager.

sre-bot: [action] created incident INC-2026-0345: "eu-west standby swap led to tokenizer mismatch" assigned=neha_sre priority=high

sam_support: filing billing ticket to credit ACME for duplicate token charges (TICKET-7890). Can SRE confirm the affected request_ids so finance can calculate credit? I'll attach logs.

neha_sre: pulling full list now, grep on `tokenizer_vocab_mismatch` and the timeframe 2026-03-16T14:20:00Z..14:26:00Z. preliminary list: rq_0ab9f3e2, rq_0b39dff1, rq_0c12a9b7. Will update INC-2026-0345 with final list and expected credit amount estimate.

leo_prod: follow-ups — I'll block the standby variant in the model catalog for generation family and kick an urgent config rollback. Also will add a canary test that exercises tokenizer compatibility before mapping variants into standby groups.

sam_support: thanks. I'll message the customer with interim update and the billing ticket. Please ping here once rollback is done so I can confirm customer tests. :thumbsup:
